g.text: aq watches every Claude Code session in your tmux and puts
whatever needs you in one queue, shown one card at a time:
a diff to review, an edit to allow, a permission prompt.
This tour takes about two minutes, and you get to try it.
skip the tour (F2 brings it back)
❯ the API's rate limit is one shared window; make it a token bucket per key
aq watches every Claude Code session in your tmux and puts
whatever needs you in one queue, shown one card at a time:
This tour takes about two minutes, and you get to try it.
aq hears from Claude through three hooks in
~/.claude/settings.json; the README shows how to add them,
or has a prompt you can paste to Claude to do it for you.
Sessions started before the hooks were added need a restart.
Without aq running, the hooks do nothing at all.
The top bar counts what is waiting behind the card on screen.
Decide on a card and the next one comes up.
move, as in vim (also Ctrl-d, Ctrl-u, gg, G)
A card that jumps in ignores deciding keys for 1.5 s, so a
key meant for the last card never lands on the new one.
Each project (git checkout) has its own mode.
when a session finishes, review its diff
every edit waits for you before it is applied
explain parts of the change in your own words
move the project to the next mode
Next comes a practice review card, made up for this tour.
It is what you get when a session finishes a turn.
The tour tells you which key to press, one at a time.
Nothing you do on it reaches a real session.
leave the tour, during the practice too
to move down a line (k moves up)
to go to the next file (H goes back)
to switch between the split and unified views
to comment on the line under the cursor
to save it, once you have typed a few words
to mark this file done: it is ticked and skipped from now on
to send your comments to the session as one message
to approve the change, which closes the card
That was review mode. In step mode each edit is its own card:
send it back with a reason Claude sees
In quiz mode a box opens on each question:
after the verdict: keep as is, or ask for a fix
Practice: approved, and the card is gone
You get a tab per session, with the picked one's screen live.
message it (sent once it is idle)
ask where it is up to, without interrupting it
ask it to open a pull request
ask the session a side question; a copy answers
start a new Claude session in this project
a shell in a popup, with Claude's last ! command typed in
select text; letting go copies it
That's it. F2 shows this tour again.
